title: Paths and project trees

sources.locator: Pro Git; second edition online; section applicable to Paths and project trees
sources.claim: Shell commands resolve relative paths from the current working directory, while absolute paths begin at a filesystem root; dot and dot-dot name current and parent locations.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Every terminal has a **current working directory**, shown by `pwd`. A **relative path** like `src/app.js` or `../README.md` is resolved **from there**, not from the project root. An **absolute path** starts at the top of the filesystem: `/home/asha/project` on macOS and Linux, `C:\Users\Asha\project` on Windows. Two special names help: `.` means "this folder" and `..` means "the parent folder"; `~` usually means your home folder. Put paths with **spaces** in quotes, and remember some systems (Linux) treat `README.md` and `readme.md` as different files while others (Windows, default macOS) don't.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner is inside `repo/src` in the terminal and types `cat ./README.md`, expecting the project README. The terminal says the file doesn't exist, although they can see README.md in the editor's sidebar. From repo/src, ../README.md resolves to the README in repo, while ./README.md looks inside src and may not exist. In this lesson you'll navigate and explain a nested project tree without relying on the current GUI location.

```predict
{"question": "You're in /home/asha/repo/src. Where does `../docs/guide.md` point?", "options": ["/home/asha/repo/src/docs/guide.md", "/home/asha/repo/docs/guide.md"], "answer": 1, "why": ".. goes up one level from the current directory, to repo, then into docs."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Files, folders and paths**: files, folders and how a project is organised into a tree.

sections.heading: The model: start where you are, or start at the root
sections.body:
```bash
pwd                        # print the current working directory.
# /home/asha/repo/src

ls ..                      # list the parent folder (repo).
cat ../README.md           # relative: up one level, then README.md.
cat /home/asha/repo/README.md   # absolute: same file from anywhere.

cd ..                      # move up to repo.
cd "my notes"              # quotes keep a name with a space together.
cd ~                       # home folder.
cd -                       # back to the previous folder (bash, zsh).
```

```text
repo/                      <- ..  when you are in src
  README.md
  docs/
    guide.md
  src/                     <- .   (current working directory)
    app.js
```

| Path | Starts from |
|---|---|
| `app.js` or `./app.js`. | the current directory. |
| `../README.md`. | the parent of the current directory. |
| `/home/asha/repo`. | the filesystem root (absolute). |
| `C:\Users\Asha\repo`. | a drive root on Windows (absolute). |
| `~/repo`. | your home folder. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Does the editor's open folder change the terminal's directory?", "answer": "No. They're separate. Always check the terminal with pwd before running commands that use relative paths."}
```

sections.heading: Spaces and case

includes: Resolve relative, absolute, parent (..) and home (~) paths from the current directory.
Quote paths with spaces and account for case sensitivity.

outcomes: Navigate and explain a nested project tree without relying on the current GUI location.

examples.title: Which README did I just open?
examples.situation: From repo/src, ../README.md resolves to the README in repo, while ./README.md looks inside src and may not exist.
walkthrough: **Check where you are:** pwd prints /home/asha/repo/src, so relative paths start in src.
**Resolve:** ./README.md means repo/src/README.md, which doesn't exist; ../README.md goes up to repo.
**Verify:** the learner will run `ls ..` to see README.md listed, then `cat ../README.md` prints the project README.
examples.result: The learner opens the right README from any folder, without relying on the editor's sidebar.

examples.title: The script that only worked from the root
examples.situation: A teammate's instructions say `node scripts/build.js`. It works from the repo root but fails from repo/src with "Cannot find module".
walkthrough: The path is relative to the current directory.
Either cd to the repo root first, or use ../scripts/build.js from src.
examples.result: The build runs from wherever the learner is, because they resolve the path deliberately.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every relative path starts from the repository root, regardless of the terminal's current working directory.
misconceptions.correction: Relative paths are resolved from the terminal's current working directory, which can be any subfolder. Check it with pwd, or use an absolute path when in doubt.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Which README did I just open?", where did ./README.md point?

analogy.example: A relative path is like **directions from where you're standing**: "go out this door and turn left" depends on which room you're in. An absolute path is **a full postal address** that works from anywhere. `..` is "step out into the corridor".
limitations: Rooms don't move; your terminal's location does every time you cd.
Case-sensitive systems treat Room A and room a as different doors.

steps.explanation: The learner checks the current working directory first.
From repo/src, ./README.md looks inside src and may not exist.
../README.md resolves to the README in repo.

trace.textAlternative: Resolving paths from a subfolder. Step 1, Locate: current directory is repo/src. The learner checks the current working directory first. Step 2, Wrong path: ./README.md is repo/src/README.md; result is No such file. From repo/src, ./README.md looks inside src and may not exist. Step 3, Right path: ../README.md is repo/README.md; result is file printed. ../README.md resolves to the README in repo.

nearTransfer.prompt: You're in /home/asha/repo/docs. Write the relative path to repo/src/app.js and the absolute path to the same file. Then give the command to go home and come back.
expectedEvidence: cd ~, then cd - returns to docs.

farTransfer.prompt: Create a disposable folder tree with a folder named "study notes" and a file README.md at two levels. Navigate only with the terminal, printing pwd before each command, and read each README with both a relative and an absolute path.
scaffold: Record each command and its output.
expectedEvidence: A short note on where each relative path started.

remediation.explanation: Before any command with a path, run **pwd** and say out loud: **"this path starts from ___"**. If you're unsure, use an absolute path or `ls` the folder first.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The script that only worked from the root".

recap.summary: To navigate and explain a project tree, check the current working directory with pwd, resolve relative paths from there (. for here, .. for the parent, ~ for home), use absolute paths from the root when location is uncertain, quote paths containing spaces, and remember case sensitivity varies by system.
retrievalPrompts: Where does a relative path start?
Why quote a path with spaces?
